h3. Driver is manually blocked due to document review in the UK and IE

*Rejected documents*

* When the Ops team reject a document, they should leave a reason for the scheduled block
* If a reason is not given, check the _Change log_ to confirm the status of the document and follow the relevant next step:
** *Rejected*: Escalate the case via the escalation form
** *Verified*: If you see an active block under the Scheduled blocking tab, escalate to Tier-2 and go to [Driver is automatically blocked due to document issues|#driver-is-automatically-blocked-due-to-document-issues] section

🇬🇧 *UK*

* If the blocking reason is *Under investigation* or *Document quality*
** Escalate the case to the [UK Ops Compliance Team’s SD|https://taxify.atlassian.net/servicedesk/customer/portal/31/group/107/create/529] and proceed according to their instructions
** *Note*: Don’t invite drivers to the Hub if they are blocked. 

🇮🇪 *Ireland*

* In the driver's Admin profile, check the _Change log_ to see how long ago the driver uploaded the document and proceed based on the timeline: 
** *Less than 24 hours passed*: Inform the driver we have received their documents and our Operations team will review them as soon as possible
** *More than 24 hours passed*: Escalate the case to Local OPS team via Beehive 

h4. Driver is blocked due to missing or invalid documents or NIN

If the driver’s account was blocked due to the *DVLA disqualifications*:

* Escalate the case to the Compliance team via the UK Ops Service Desk and proceed based on their instructions. 
* Wait for their comment or solution and proceed accordingly.
* If the driver doesn’t have a *fully renewed licence* and they are licensed in one of the cities below the extension letter can be accepted. Advise them to upload the needed documents via Driver Portal:
** *Birmingham*: expired licence/badge + extension letter
** *Sandwell*: expired licence/badge + extension letter
** *Solihull*: temporary licence + expired badge + extension letter
** *Milton Keynes*: expired licence/badge + extension letter/emai
** *Salford*: extension with the current PHV +extension letter with the CoC
** *Edinburgh*: PHL (private hire car licence or taxi licence if vehicle is licensed for private hire), PHV, CoC have extension letters.

*Private hire vehicle*

Drivers waiting for the renewal in *Edinburgh*

* We can accept the CoC but it must be issued after the previous PHV was issued. The previous PHV must be in Admin or proof of the licence on the Ediburgh Council online register 
* We can accept the renewal application and we can also accept the email confirmation of the renewal
* If the driver has technical issues submitting a renewed document, the reason the submitted document was rejected remains unclear, or the driver is blocked even after the required document was accepted escalate the case to the relevant team and proceed based on their instructions .	
** *London*: Escalate to the [Reactivation team via Service Desk|https://taxify.atlassian.net/servicedesk/customer/portal/35]
** *Expansion*: Escalate to [Expansion via Service Desk|https://taxify.atlassian.net/servicedesk/customer/portal/31/create/528?src=1826823624]

h4. Block with the reason _Good for review_

* The driver must pass compliance checks before the block is removed
* Once these checks are done, the local OPS team will remove the block.

h4. Pending review blocks

* This is applied when a driver has uploaded a new document and it has been verified by an agent but has not yet been reviewed and approved by the Compliance team
* It can take up to 24 hours for the block to be removed.

h4. Vehicle suspended by Council block

* Advise the driver to get in touch with the Council
** Drivers must confirm with the Council that we can proceed with the unblocking
** The council should communicate the decision to the local OPS team.
** Drivers must confirm with the Council that this information was sent to us
* It can take up to 24 hours for the block to be removed

Bonjour Gregory,

*Demande d'accès à des données personnelles - Réponse*

Merci pour votre demande d'accès aux données personnelles, qui a été reçue par nous le *8/5/2024*.

Après avoir effectué une recherche diligente des dossiers relatifs à votre demande d'accès, nous avons confirmé que nous traitons les données personnelles demandées. 

Nous partageons une copie des données personnelles que nous détenons à votre sujet et auxquelles vous avez droit, y compris :

* l'historique de vos déplacements en 2023

Nous tenons à préciser que nous ne conservons pas de données kilométriques agrégées. Nous joignons une copie de votre historique de voyage pour la période spécifiée afin de faciliter les calculs qui peuvent être effectués indépendamment.

Vous pouvez obtenir votre distance totale mensuelle via le portail Bolt Driver Portal. Il vous suffit de naviguer vers « Mes trajets », de spécifier le mois souhaité et le système affichera les données pertinentes, y compris la « distance totale » en kilomètres.

En vertu de la loi sur la protection de la vie privée, nous ne sommes pas autorisés à générer une nouvelle représentation des données pour répondre à votre demande d'accès. Nous vous remercions de votre compréhension et vous prions de nous excuser pour les désagréments que cela pourrait occasionner.

Pour plus d'informations sur la manière dont nous traitons les données personnelles pertinentes, nous vous renvoyons à notre [Politique de confidentialité pour les Partenaires Chauffeurs |https://bolt.eu/fr-fr/privacy/privacy-for-drivers/?category=rides], qui comprend de plus amples informations sur :

* Les catégories de données personnelles que nous traitons ;
* Les finalités pour lesquelles nous traitons les données personnelles ;
* Les destinataires ou catégories de destinataires auxquels les données personnelles ont été ou seront divulguées ;
* Les critères que nous utilisons pour déterminer la durée de conservation des données à caractère personnel ;
* Les sources de données à caractère personnel reçues d'autres parties ;
* Vos droits relatifs à vos données à caractère personnel ;
* L'existence et les conséquences envisagées de toute prise de décision automatisée/de tout profilage de données à caractère personnel ; et
* Les détails de tout transfert de vos données à caractère personnel vers des pays tiers ou des organisations internationales et les garanties utilisées pour de tels transferts.

*Vos droits*

Outre votre droit d'accès aux données à caractère personnel que nous détenons à votre sujet, vous avez le droit de nous demander de rectifier, d'effacer vos données à caractère personnel, de restreindre le traitement de vos données à caractère personnel ou de vous opposer à un tel traitement. Toutes les demandes de ce type qui sont reçues seront examinées en conjonction avec les dispositions applicables des lois pertinentes sur la protection des données.

Si vous n'êtes pas satisfait de la réponse à votre demande ou de toute autre question relative au traitement de vos données à caractère personnel, nous espérons que vous continuerez à travailler avec nous pour les résoudre. Vous avez également le droit de vous plaindre directement auprès de votre autorité de protection des données/supervision et, en fonction des lois sur la protection des données applicables dans votre pays, de demander un recours judiciaire.

Si vous avez d'autres questions, veuillez contacter notre équipe d'assistance à la clientèle en répondant à cet e-mail.

Cordialement,

Bolt

Thank you for your data subject request, which was received by us on *8/5/2024.*

 

After conducting a diligent search for records relating to your access request, we have confirmed that we do process the personal data requested. 

We are sharing a copy of the personal data we hold about *you* to which you are entitled, including:

* The existence and envisaged consequences of any automated decision-making/profiling of personal data; and

*Your rights*

You also have the right to complain directly to your data protection/supervisory authority and, depending on the applicable data protection laws in your country, to seek a judicial remedy.

 

If you have any additional questions, please contact our Customer Support Team by replying to this email.

 

Yours sincerely,

Bolt

Hi [~accountid:61e918be38041c00686ad2bf] , [~accountid:622852f26a4c4c0070b16e66], [~accountid:5b76bc2cb974540708ee16ee]  

We received feedback from Osborne Clarke [+here+|https://docs.google.com/document/d/1OQqCp3rTBVLhCb6NNnkmVRQLk3DIAQJF/edit] is their full advice. Pls find below a summary incorporating an overview of the reclassification risks in FR and general internal guidance on the broader (regular) Branding which is also relevant to Hertz-for-Bolt Branding.



Overview: 

{color:#0747a6}+*_France’s risk profile_*+{color}

Although there’s no existing regulation dedicated to platform workers employment status in France nor ‘presumption criteria law’,  drivers can enforce existing Labour law provisions and seek the reclassification of their service agreement into an employment contract (for more details, see relevant GOAT pages), if the following criteria/ elements are fulfilled :

* the provision of work,
* the payment of a remuneration, and
* the existence of a ‘relationship (or link) of subordination’ - meaning that they perform the services under the authority of an employer who has the power to give orders and instructions, to control their execution and to sanction any breach by his subordinate’. Following factual elements have been considered as indications of a relationship (or link) of subordination:
** any element showing the platform’s power of control, management and (direct and/or indirect) sanction towards the driver, such as the existence of orders/directives and a system of sanctions in case of inexecution;
** elements suggesting that the independent contractor is a member of the company;
** the lack of freedom in developing their own business customers;
** prices imposed by a platform.



Due to the above and considering the court assessments in FR recognising employment status of  RH platform workers in some cases, France is considered to be the highest risk class (*Class 3/3*) market according to GOAT (internal tool to evaluate risks). F*or these reasons, France  is clearly a market with material reclassification concerns. Therefore any initiative aiming at facilitating drivers’ access to their main working tool, controlling/ or giving the impression to control somehow the appearance or autonomy of drivers, incentivising branding with bonuses (and in case cases performance targets) must be carefully assessed.*  



# {color:#0747a6}*Branding* {color}

In the event of a litigation, having a branded car would not constitute _per se_ strong grounds to claim for the reclassification of the commercial contractual relationship between the Driver and the Platform into an employment contract. Associated risks are limited for Bolt, insofar *Bolt does not impose any obligation to put the sticker* on the Drivers’ cars and *branding is offered on an opt-in basis without any direct sanctions imposed if the Driver opts out.*

 

*However*, the judges could consider that Bolt indirectly imposes some *sanctions* on the Drivers who are not willing to rent a branded car and who are essentially penalised by not receiving  the branding bonus. Moreover, judges could argue that Bolt exercises its *disciplinary power to control* the status of the logo, notably by asking the drivers to send pictures of branded cars.



{color:#0747a6}*1.1 Herts- for-Bolt  Branding consideration & payment*{color}

_In the below paragraph Scenario A and Scenario B are two schemes  and should be intended as follows:_ 

*_Scenario A_*_: fixed amount (granted even if the Driver performs 0 rides)+ kickback commission on performed rides._

*_Scenario B_*_: fixed amount up to 180 euros._ 



*OC considers that scenario A is less risky than scenario B*, since drivers will receive separately a fixed amount of the drives provided, and kickback commissions for the branding service provided. Please find additional details in the memo for Branded cars already shared with Local Ops.     

*Mitigation*: 

* *paying drivers a fixed amount* even if they do not perform any rides for Bolt (before the withdrawal of the branding in case of use of the “backstop” of the utilisation guarantee);
* issuing *two separate invoices* (for transportation services and advertising services - ie branding) and insert the narrative “advertising services” not bonuses.
* choose a *payment frequency other than on a* +*monthly*+ *basis* which is usually the frequency of wages payment for employees. Indeed, independent workers are supposed to be paid once they have provided the services, upon receipt of their invoices.



+*Bolt internal guidance from Product Legal +GFT  on top of OC’s advice:*+

* +*_Avoiding performance targets_*++_:_+ Bolt can de-risk the initiative by ensuring that no ‘special targets’ or ‘incentives’ specifically apply to these vehicles / fleets / drivers. In effect, the vehicles are subject to the same requirements as any other vehicle and there are no ‘sweeteners / requirements’ to using them, beyond the commercial deal of “£££ <---> get the car”. Having exclusive performance targets / incentives to branded vehicles will escalate the risk profile as they can be reasonably argued to evidence a wider pattern of economic / performance based control. Considering that the ‘overall aesthetic’ of these vehicles is already striking, this is something that Bolt should aim to accommodate in any ‘risky’ market (such as France).
* +*_Treat all branded vehicles in the same way_*+ Bolt can further mitigate the impact by ensuring that Hertz-for-Bolt branded vehicles are not  given any preferential treatment above any other branded vehicle (no dispatch priority, no exclusive bonuses etc.).
* +*Branding design and legal disclaimer*+*:* hard legal requirement is to insert a  legal disclaimer on car stating : "*_Publicité pour la centrale de réservation Bolt_**".*  +Nota: branding in FR qualifies as+ +*advertising services.*+

{color:#0747a6}*1.2 Payment flow*{color}: the fact that drivers will mandate Bolt to reverse the money to Hertz could be considered evidence /showing that drivers are integrated into an organised service (Bolt), on top of the provision of a working tool (ie the car), thus showing an employment relationship.  

At a later stage, Bolt could consider facilitating the car rent payment by allowing drivers to mandate Bolt to reverse part of the money paid by passengers to Hertz to pay the car rent.

*Mitigation*: if such an option is implemented in the future (_subject to further Financial Regulation clearance by Gerly)_, OC recommend that Bolt provides a *mechanism which can demonstrate that drivers formally decide to give Bolt a mandate to pay out this mone*_y,_ so that Bolt can be seen as a mere business partner facilitating the business relationship between drivers and Hertz.



# {color:#0747a6}*Utilisation guarantee for branded cars*{color}

The fact that Bolt will cover the loss of revenue (rent) related to the reduced use of the branded cars (up to the guarantee amount of €3,000 per car), could be considered as an element showing an employment relationship between the driver and Bolt since such financial risks are generally borne by an employer for their employees, or directly borne by self-employed workers; 

*Mitigation/ counter arguments*: Bolt could argue that we are rather bearing the financial risks of Hertz. Indeed if Hertz does not rent out the vehicles as planned, they would incur in financial losses that we are partially compensating via the Guarantee. 



# {color:#0747a6}*Cumulating Academy + Hertz program*{color}{color:#0747a6} {color}{color:#0747a6}*with a branded vehicle*{color} 

OC would assess the *risks to be of about 30%* (i.e., *10% risk* related to the implementation of the Ride Hailing Rental Program with Hertz *in addition to the 20% risk assessed for the Bolt Academy Project)*.





*Conclusion*: in light of OC assessment, this program does not raise material risks in addition to the ones already outlined in relation to regular Branding, to the extent Bolt is able to accommodate the suggested mitigation measures and accept some level of risk. 

However, considering FR is a high reclassification risk market, the Business should make its decision to proceed in this market on the basis that :

(i)it is making a well-informed, calculated decision cannot, 

(ii) the commercial benefits outweigh the risk profile, and 

(iii)has done all that it practically can to de-risk. 



Please let me know if you need additional clarification and let me know if the Business provides final sign off on the programme. 



*In terms of next steps*, I will continue supporting the contract negotiation and will wait for your instructions to adjust our French Branding terms to create some bespoke templates to be implemented in Hertz car booking flow for Driver’s acceptance.

Thanks,

Michela

Hi [~accountid:5da0457ec62f840db2b704a9], 

As per our T&Cs the following is applicable: 

* 1.2 . The passenger (you) enters into a contract with the driver for the provision of transport services via the Bolt app. +Depending on the payment options supported for given location of the journey, you can choose whether to pay the driver for the transport service in cash or use Bolt in-App Payment+.

For Finland, currently cash payments are not supported which means that according to our T&Cs you can *only pay via Bolt in-App Payments in Finland*. 

* 3.1 Depending on the payment options supported for the given location of the journey, You can pay for the transport services with a card, mobile carrier billing or other payment methods (e.g: Bolt Business) as and when available through Bolt App. +By providing Bolt in-App Payment service, Bolt acts as commercial agent for the providers of the transport services+. Every driver has authorised Bolt as their commercial agent for the mediation of conclusion of contracts between the driver and the passenger, including the power to accept payments from the passengers and to forward the payments to the driver. Your obligation to the provider of the transport service will be fulfilled when the payment order is given to transfer funds to Bolts’ bank account. +You, as a passenger are responsible for ensuring that the payment takes place+ and ensuring that sufficient funds are available.

Bolt is acting as an agent for payment purposes between the driver and rider. Bolt however can’t control if the driver and rider agree to make a separate payment outside of the Bolt app. Such a payment is completely outside of the control of Bolt. *Since the in-App Payment was refunded, the customer has already been refunded for the “double-charge”* and the separate card payment can be seen as payment for the trip which was agreed between the parties separately. 

*It is up to you to decide if you still want to give the customer an extra refund to keep the customer happy but from a legal standpoint we don’t have an obligation to do so*. We should remind the rider that we only support in-App Payments and that if they book a ride via the Bolt App the payment will be made in the App so that no separate payment is required.

{code:sql}WITH finished_orders AS (
SELECT 
co.user_id,
APPROX_DISTINCT(co.id,0.0041) AS count_finished_orders
FROM ng_public.etl_denormalized_commerce_orders co 
WHERE co.created_date >= date '2023-01-01'
AND co.order_type = 'rides'
AND co.order_state = 'finished'
GROUP BY 1 
)
SELECT 
date(date_trunc('month',a.created)) AS month,
--TRUNCATE(DATE_DIFF('day',u.created,a.created),-1) AS user_age,
--TRUNCATE(COALESCE(fo.count_finished_orders,0),-1) AS finished_orders,
APPROX_DISTINCT(a.id,0.0041) AS count_fraud_checks,
APPROX_DISTINCT(CASE WHEN a.decision.decision = 'REJECT' THEN a.id END,0.0041) AS count_rejects,
ROUND(CAST(APPROX_DISTINCT(CASE WHEN a.decision.decision = 'REJECT' THEN a.id END,0.0041)*1.000/APPROX_DISTINCT(a.id,0.0041) AS double),3) AS reject_ratio,
APPROX_DISTINCT(a.meta.user_id,0.0041) AS count_dist_users,
APPROX_DISTINCT(CASE WHEN a.decision.decision = 'REJECT' THEN a.meta.user_id END,0.0041) AS count_dist_rejected_users,
ROUND(CAST(APPROX_DISTINCT(CASE WHEN a.decision.decision = 'REJECT' THEN a.meta.user_id END,0.0041)*1.000/APPROX_DISTINCT(a.meta.user_id,0.0041) AS double),3) AS user_reject_ratio,
ROUND(CAST(APPROX_DISTINCT(CASE WHEN a.decision.decision = 'REJECT' THEN a.id END,0.0041)*1.000/NULLIF(APPROX_DISTINCT(CASE WHEN a.decision.decision = 'REJECT' THEN a.meta.user_id END,0.0041),0) AS double),3) AS rejects_per_user
FROM archive_analytical.campaign_targeting_batch_enrolment a
--JOIN ng_public.user_user u ON u.id = a.meta.user_id
LEFT JOIN finished_orders fo ON fo.user_id = a.meta.user_id
WHERE a.created_hour >= date '2024-01-01'
AND COALESCE(fo.count_finished_orders,0) = 0 
GROUP BY 1--,2
ORDER BY 1 DESC{code}

“Hi [_]

_To be clear, Bolt operates as an independent data controller when providing services to its business customers. Our_ [+_General Terms and Conditions for Bolt Business_+|https://bolt.eu/en-th/legal/terms-for-bolt-business/?category=boltBusiness] _Section 4 states explicitly that Bolt and the business customer maintain their independent data controller roles for personal data processing. Bolt fully assumes responsibility for its processing activities and adherence to applicable laws, including the GDPR. This covers areas such as engaging subprocessors, implementing necessary security measures, and establishing data retention periods._

_When a business customer`s employee or any data subject uses Bolt Business services for a ride, they are treated as a regular user of the Bolt Rider App. The experience of these business users is identical to that of regular users, except for the availability of an alternative payment option (Bolt Business) and an additional ride category (Business Ride). This may result in a scenario where, if a business customer deactivates and removes a business user's account, this individual will lose access to an alternative payment option (Bolt Business) and an additional ride category (Business Ride)._

In practical terms, this means that the personal data provided by business customers is  used to match newly added business users with the accounts of standard users. * hypothesis 4
** idea is that fraudsters related to *card_adding* checkpoint create thousands of accounts and get stopped by us and churn. after a while, they get targeted by Campaigns with the goal of reactivating them.

{code:sql}WITH card_adding_sus_users AS (
SELECT 
a.meta.user_id AS user_id
FROM archive_analytical.user_payment_instrument_adding_check a
WHERE a.created_hour >= date '2024-01-01'
AND a.decision.decision IN ('reject','challenge')
GROUP BY 1 
)
SELECT 
date(date_trunc('month',a.created)) AS month,
APPROX_DISTINCT(a.id,0.0041) AS count_fraud_checks,
APPROX_DISTINCT(CASE WHEN a.decision.decision = 'REJECT' THEN a.id END,0.0041) AS count_rejects,
ROUND(CAST(APPROX_DISTINCT(CASE WHEN a.decision.decision = 'REJECT' THEN a.id END,0.0041)*1.000/APPROX_DISTINCT(a.id,0.0041) AS double),3) AS reject_ratio,
APPROX_DISTINCT(a.meta.user_id,0.0041) AS count_dist_users,
APPROX_DISTINCT(CASE WHEN a.decision.decision = 'REJECT' THEN a.meta.user_id END,0.0041) AS count_dist_rejected_users,
ROUND(CAST(APPROX_DISTINCT(CASE WHEN a.decision.decision = 'REJECT' THEN a.meta.user_id END,0.0041)*1.000/APPROX_DISTINCT(a.meta.user_id,0.0041) AS double),3) AS user_reject_ratio,
ROUND(CAST(APPROX_DISTINCT(CASE WHEN a.decision.decision = 'REJECT' THEN a.id END,0.0041)*1.000/NULLIF(APPROX_DISTINCT(CASE WHEN a.decision.decision = 'REJECT' THEN a.meta.user_id END,0.0041),0) AS double),3) AS rejects_per_user
FROM archive_analytical.campaign_targeting_batch_enrolment a
JOIN card_adding_sus_users c ON c.user_id = a.meta.user_id
WHERE a.created_hour >= date '2024-01-01'
GROUP BY 1
ORDER BY 1 DESC{code}

definitely an increase, but still a minimal contribution to the whole pool of rejected users.

There are no restricted Fivetran tables at the moment. Fivetran exports data into a “public" bucket, which everyone has access to via, e.g., Databricks' common workspace. Setting granular restrictive permissions on such a widely used bucket is cumbersome and risky, as it can break existing accesses and expose unwanted ones. So, if we would like to introduce Fivetran sync with restricted access, that would require a new flow and probably tooling for that. 

We can not rely on quickly truncating tables if the data in the table is really sensitive.

I re-ran the numbers with the following query:

{code:sql}WITH count_predictions AS (
SELECT 
p.order_id,
p.city_id, 
COUNT(*) AS count_predictions
FROM ng_public.pricing_order_prediction p
WHERE p.created_date >= date '2023-01-01'
GROUP BY 1,2
HAVING COUNT(*) > 1 
),
multiple_destinations AS (
SELECT 
c.order_id,
c.city_id, 
COUNT(*) AS count_destinations
FROM ng_public.company_order_destination c
WHERE c.created_date >= date '2023-01-01'
GROUP BY 1,2
HAVING COUNT(*) > 1
)
SELECT 
date(date_trunc('month',co.created)) AS month,
APPROX_DISTINCT(co.id,0.0041) AS count_orders,
APPROX_DISTINCT(CASE WHEN co.initial_failed_payment_amount > 0 OR co.is_initial_failed_payment THEN co.id END,0.0041) AS count_initial_fp,
ROUND(CAST(APPROX_DISTINCT(CASE WHEN co.initial_failed_payment_amount > 0 OR co.is_initial_failed_payment THEN co.id END,0.0041)*1.000/APPROX_DISTINCT(co.id,0.0041) AS double),3) AS initial_fp_count_ratio,
APPROX_DISTINCT(CASE WHEN co.uncovered_amount > 0 OR co.is_final_failed_payment THEN co.id END,0.0041) AS count_fp,
ROUND(CAST(APPROX_DISTINCT(CASE WHEN co.uncovered_amount > 0 OR co.is_final_failed_payment THEN co.id END,0.0041)*1.000/APPROX_DISTINCT(co.id,0.0041) AS double),3) AS fp_count_ratio,
ROUND(CAST(SUM(co.user_price_eur) AS double),2) AS sum_user_price_eur,
ROUND(CAST(SUM(co.initial_failed_payment_amount/co.eur_currency_rate) AS double),2) AS sum_initial_fp,
ROUND(CAST(ROUND(CAST(SUM(co.initial_failed_payment_amount/co.eur_currency_rate) AS double),2)*1.000/ROUND(CAST(SUM(co.user_price_eur) AS double),2) AS double),3) AS initial_fp_sum_ratio,
ROUND(CAST(SUM(co.uncovered_amount/co.eur_currency_rate) AS double),2) AS sum_fp,
ROUND(CAST(ROUND(CAST(SUM(co.uncovered_amount/co.eur_currency_rate) AS double),2)*1.000/ROUND(CAST(SUM(co.user_price_eur) AS double),2) AS double),3) AS fp_sum_ratio
FROM ng_public.etl_denormalized_commerce_orders co
JOIN multiple_destinations md ON md.order_id = co.order_id AND md.city_id = co.city_id 
JOIN count_predictions cp ON cp.order_id = co.order_id AND cp.city_id = co.city_id 
WHERE co.created_date >= date '2023-01-01'
AND co.order_type = 'rides'
AND co.order_state = 'finished'
AND co.card_booked_amount > 0
GROUP BY 1 
ORDER BY 1 DESC {code}

* Storno invoice (correction) - reverse the Original invoice (incorrect) to Business Company A
* Reissue invoice (correction) - to Business Company B
* Charge (correction) - to Business Company B

Dear Mariana

 

*Data Subject Access Request – Response* 

 

Thank you for your data subject request, which was received by us on 14 May 2024.

 

After conducting a diligent search for records relating to your access request, we have confirmed that we do process the personal data requested. In the current implementation, the change in the database structure is captured by the [skeema|https://www.skeema.io/] utility on the {{Verify}} step in the Jenkins pipeline. the {{yarn db-diff:current}} yarn command creates all databases in a container on the MySQL server and runs a skeema tool against it. *this means the TiDB dialect is not supported.*

On top of that, the SQLFluff used in the db-schema-change repository as an SQL linter does not support TiDB dialect.

TiDB suggests another way of setting a TTL, compatible with the MYSQL dialect - [https://docs.pingcap.com/tidb/stable/time-to-live/|https://docs.pingcap.com/tidb/stable/time-to-live/|smart-link]. But SQL-level comments are not tracked by the skeema tool.

The solution could be:

* Wait for Juri to update tidb image to 7.5 - [https://taxify.slack.com/archives/C046TK6FZ7Z/p1718110921191749|https://taxify.slack.com/archives/C046TK6FZ7Z/p1718110921191749|smart-link]

* To update db-diff step, options:
** To use MySQL and TiDB db containers separately for different database types
** diff update
*** replace skeema with the home-made tool
*** OR find a tool supporting tidb dialect
**** [https://docs.pingcap.com/tidb/stable/sync-diff-inspector-overview|https://docs.pingcap.com/tidb/stable/sync-diff-inspector-overview|smart-link] with {{check-struct-only = true}} flag
*** OR contribute to skeema opensource project to implement TiDB dialect
* Update db-schema-change linter to support TiDB dialect, options:
** Find a TiDB dialect-compatible linter
** contribute to the SqlFluff opensource project to implement TiDB dialect

Overall, the path of least efforts would be:

# wait for Juri
# replace skeema with sync-diff-inspector tool
# fork and implement tidb support for the SqlFluff
# update db-schema-change GH linter action to use updated SqlFluff

Hello Dominik Dutko 

We should not reissue any invoice upon request for the reasons like no NIP number at the time of issuance and a rider providing the number later, or a rider requesting a change of address or name later on. It is not allowed by the VAT law to reissue invoices for these reasons.

Unless it is our mistake, e.g. the value, subject of the sale, or NIP number is wrongly stated by us, then we reissue the invoice. And we need to report VAT for the new invoice.

So if the rider requests to reissue the invoice for their own sake in the future, +you can tell them+ +*according to art., 106b ust. 6 VAT law in Poland*++, we are not allowed to do so.+

*More indices VS less indices*

{quote}(If possible to support more indices, then we may support more complicated search requests. If not, then we need to do some trade-offs)

* Is it easy/doable to add new column or new INDEX to existing big table in TiDB? (big table is a table with total size > 1TB){quote}

It is doable, however building or re-organizing index still requires some time and resources. Compared to MySQL it happens in the background and implementation is different. Therefore there’s few magnitudes less effect on live operations and it’s very unlikely that the DDL will fail to complete. 

Also see: [https://docs.pingcap.com/tidb/stable/sql-faq#how-does-tidb-perform-when-executing-ddl-operations-on-a-large-table|https://docs.pingcap.com/tidb/stable/sql-faq#how-does-tidb-perform-when-executing-ddl-operations-on-a-large-table|smart-link] 

{quote}* Does more table indices mean slower INSERTs in that table in TiDB? (Or can TiDB update indices in parallel?){quote}

There is no simple answer here. In general - it will be slower, but it’s not necessarily will be noticeable in terms of overall query performance.

Some details:

{noformat}Having more table indices generally means slower `INSERT` operations in TiDB (as well as in other database management systems). This is because each `INSERT` operation must not only add the new row to the table but also update each index associated with that table. Here’s a detailed explanation:

1. **Index Maintenance Overhead**: When a new row is inserted, the database has to update all the indices to reflect the new data. This involves locating the appropriate place in each index and inserting the new entry. If a table has multiple indices, this process is repeated for each index, adding to the time complexity.

2. **Write Amplification**: Each index requires a separate write operation. With more indices, the number of write operations increases, which can lead to higher I/O overhead and thus slower overall `INSERT` performance.

3. **Concurrency Control**: In a distributed database like TiDB, maintaining consistency across multiple indices can require additional synchronization and locking mechanisms. This can lead to increased contention and slower `INSERT` operations, especially in high-concurrency environments.

4. **Transaction Overhead**: TiDB uses a distributed transaction model, which includes two-phase commit (2PC) for ensuring atomicity and consistency. More indices mean more data needs to be locked and committed within each transaction, potentially increasing the transaction duration and resource consumption.

5. **Data Distribution**: TiDB splits data into multiple regions, and each region can be distributed across different nodes. Managing indices across these regions adds complexity, and more indices mean more metadata to manage, which can slow down `INSERT` operations due to the added coordination required.

However, it's important to balance between `INSERT` performance and query performance. Indices are crucial for speeding up read operations (e.g., `SELECT` queries), so while more indices can slow down `INSERT` operations, they can significantly improve query performance.

### Best Practices
1. **Selective Indexing**: Only create indices that are necessary for your most important queries.
2. **Monitoring and Optimization**: Regularly monitor performance and optimize indices based on query patterns and workload characteristics.
3. **Batch Inserts**: If possible, use batch inserts to amortize the cost of index updates over multiple rows.
4. **Index Types**: Consider the types of indices and their impact. For example, unique indices might have a different performance profile compared to non-unique indices.

By carefully managing the number and types of indices, you can balance the trade-offs between `INSERT` performance and query efficiency in TiDB.

In the context of TiDB, which uses RocksDB (an LSM-tree-based storage engine), the impact of more indices on `INSERT` operations can still be significant, but the dynamics are somewhat different due to the nature of LSM (Log-Structured Merge) trees. Here’s how it works and the impact on performance:

### LSM Tree Characteristics

1. **Write Amplification**: LSM trees are designed to optimize write performance. Data is initially written to a memtable (an in-memory structure) and then flushed to disk sequentially in immutable SSTables (Sorted String Tables). This design reduces random writes but introduces write amplification during compaction (the process of merging and reorganizing SSTables).

2. **Index Management**: In an LSM-tree-based system, indices are typically also stored using LSM trees. When a new row is inserted, each index needs to be updated, similar to B-tree systems. The new index entries are written to their respective memtables and eventually flushed to SSTables.

### Impact of More Indices on INSERT Performance

1. **Increased Write Volume**: Each additional index increases the amount of data that needs to be written. Even though LSM trees are optimized for sequential writes, the overall write volume still increases with more indices, leading to higher write amplification during compaction.

2. **Compaction Overhead**: More indices mean more SSTables, which can lead to more frequent and more complex compactions. Compaction is a resource-intensive process, and more indices exacerbate this by increasing the number of SSTables that need to be merged and reorganized.

3. **Memory Usage**: Each index requires its own memtable and bloom filter in memory. More indices mean more memory usage, which can impact the overall performance of the system, especially if memory resources are constrained.

4. **Concurrency and Locking**: During the `INSERT` operation, TiDB must update multiple memtables concurrently. This can lead to contention and increased locking overhead, impacting the latency of `INSERT` operations.

### Advantages in LSM Tree Systems

1. **Sequential Write Optimization**: LSM trees are better at handling high write throughput due to their sequential write nature. This means that while more indices do slow down `INSERT` operations, the impact might be less severe compared to traditional B-tree systems.

2. **Deferred Work**: The actual work of merging and organizing data (compaction) is deferred, allowing for more efficient bulk processing. This means immediate `INSERT` operations might not be as significantly impacted as they would be in B-tree systems.

### Best Practices for LSM Tree Systems

1. **Limit Indices**: As with any system, limit the number of indices to those that are essential for query performance.
2. **Optimize Compaction**: Tune compaction strategies and parameters in RocksDB to balance between write performance and read efficiency. This can include adjusting the size of memtables, compaction thresholds, and parallelism.
3. **Monitor and Adjust**: Continuously monitor performance metrics and adjust configurations as necessary. Use tools provided by TiDB to analyze the impact of indices on write performance.
4. **Batch Operations**: Where possible, use batch insert operations to reduce the overhead per row insert and to take advantage of LSM tree write optimizations.

By understanding the specific characteristics of LSM-tree-based systems like RocksDB, you can better manage the trade-offs between `INSERT` performance and the number of indices in TiDB.
{noformat}

Hi team, 

re consent form: Adding some context for reference. 

A few months ago, we asked Privacy to advise on the best solution to collect consent for events in general following an event in Ireland. While they are working on a more extensive guide, they advised the following : 

* before the event is conducted, where possible, publicly inform that it will be filmed and for what purposes - eg., posting in social media later, and also give people an opportunity to opt out.
* This can be in the form of a simple instruction: “If you do not want to be filmed or appear in SM materials, please let the organisers know by email or approaching them on-site. If it's unclear who is the organiser, it should be clearly conveyed to the data subjects so they know whom to approach.
* *On-site, a visible banner for this would work, like A3 paper. Single consent forms where everyone gives consent to be filmed usually are not necessary*.
* Online announcements before the event would be ideal, on-site banner may not be the most practical solution, *but both approaches can be used for the same event.*
* instruct the photographer not to film children & minors, because in most situations we need an explicit consent from their parents for this.

They mentioned those rules should reduce the risks in most countries. The ticket is [here.|https://taxify.atlassian.net/servicedesk/customer/portal/47/LSS-24262] 

We used this approach for our latest driver event in March and made sure all participants were aware. The videographer was extremely visible too as the event was relatively small. 

We replicated the same strategy for this event. 

Please let us know if we need to revise this or if not applicable as the consequences for the whole strategy will be pretty painful on our end. 🥲

If you need further context, let me know. 🙏

A letter of appeal



City - Ozurgeti 

Case N 085010624001



The person making the appeal: Davit Kutateladze, investigator of the investigative division of the Guria Police Department of the Ministry of Internal Affairs of Georgia.



Content of the letter:

For execution, we are sending you the decision of the Ozurgeti District Court No. 11/A-571-24 dated 03.06.2024 regarding the request for information. Please instruct the relevant department to provide the information specified in the ruling.



Sincerely,

Davit Kutateladze





Ruling on requesting information on behalf of Georgia

03 June, 2024

City - Ozurgeti

Ozurgeti District Court Judge Ia Baramidze 



Reviewed the petition of Ozurgeti District Prosecutor Elguja Adeishvili regarding the request for information and found as follows:

The investigation is ongoing at the Guria Police Department of the Ministry of Internal Affairs of Georgia concerning Nino Nebieridze's unauthorized entry into a computer system with the intent of obtaining financial benefits, a crime specified under Part 1 of Article 286 of the Criminal Code of Georgia.

On June 3, 2024, at 5:25 p.m., Prosecutor Elguja Adeishvili petitioned the Ozurgeti District Court for permission to request complete information from the "BOLT" taxi call service application, operated by "Smartly" Ltd., associated with the email ["nucki1977@gmail.com|mailto:"nucki1977@gmail.com]" and the mobile phone number "577 760-078," regarding activities carried out on the user account registered in the name of Nino Omari's daughter, Nebieridze.

The court reviewed the petition, examined the presented materials, and concluded that the petition should be granted for the following reasons:

The court, having reviewed the petition and examined the submitted materials, believes that the collection of facts and information pertinent to the criminal case, as presented by the prosecutor, justifies the requested investigative action—the request for information—based on the following circumstances:





According to Article 9, Part 2 of the Criminal Procedure Code of Georgia, the party has the right to file a petition, obtain, request through the court, present, and examine all relevant evidence in accordance with the procedure established by this Code.

In accordance with the first part of Article 136 of the Criminal Procedure Code of Georgia, if there is a reasonable assumption that information or documents important for the criminal case are stored in a computer system or a computer data storage device, the prosecutor or the defense party is entitled to apply to the court to request the relevant information or documents. In cases of urgent necessity, the investigative action provided for in this article can be conducted based on the prosecutor's resolution, in the manner determined by Article 112, Part 5 of this Code.

According to Part 4 of the same Article, the provisions of Articles 111, 112, and 134 of this Code shall apply to the investigative action provided for in this Article.

In accordance with the first part of Article 111 of the Criminal Procedure Code of Georgia, the parties have equal rights and duties when conducting investigative actions in accordance with the procedure established by this Code. The parties conduct investigative actions in the manner and within the limits established by this Code.

Pursuant to the first part of Article 112 of the same Code, investigative actions that restrict private property, ownership, or interfere with private life are conducted based on the petition of the party and the court's decision.

In accordance with the first part of Article 94 of the same Code, if the fulfillment of the request conveyed in the petition contributes to the implementation of the tasks of the criminal justice process, it must be granted. Conversely, if the petition is aimed at delaying or hindering the criminal justice process, it must be refused.

[~accountid:628dd714269a9a0068f2a783] Going online and offline is based on driver status that is received as soon as it is being frequently updated in polling



In dynamic polling, poll_interval_sec field value triggers the next polling call. It can be configured here- [https://admin-panel.prelive.bolt.eu/fleet/drivers/edit/2803829?tab=pollSettings|https://admin-panel.prelive.bolt.eu/fleet/drivers/edit/2803829?tab=pollSettings] and tested for your user accordingly

It takes time to update to waiting for order state offline because there is a time gap between each polling interval. In live, currently it is 1.5 and 30 sec for online and offline polling, this delay in status update because it waits for 30 seconds

We can verify by giving lesser values as wait_period_summary_in_sec and offline_driver_polling_in_sec, and going offline and online will be faster. There is not any logic related bug here, but BE determines polling interval according to behaviour of dynamic polling. 

Fixed polling updated interval based on hardcoded values - 2 & 5  ,that is why we don’t see much of delay

Hey, [~accountid:712020:5c3f18cd-53ab-40ca-9fae-fb38035ab6d8]!

I have analysed the request and the law provided by [~accountid:60f2a71843c956007065f2ad]. I can see that the requesting party is Territorial Labour Inspectorate that is empowered by emergency ordinance according to Art 29 of GEO 49/2019. They are requesting information regarding drivers data related to a specific trip. According to Article 26 of GEO 49/2019 we can provide them with information. Decision no. 572/2020 article 11 prescribes that the right/obligation to make available to public institutions, in accordance with their competences, the data relating to journey, route, passengers, drivers, transport operators, car, location, contracts must be expressly specified. The request states that we shall provide information about the drivers. It does not specify what information is required, but at least it states the category of information, i.e. information about drivers and combined with the wording of Art 29 of GEO 49/2019 it seems that we can disclose all available information about “the performance of the activity” of these drivers.

Hello Julia Poniewozik 

We should not reissue any invoice upon request for the reasons like no NIP number at the time of issuance and a rider providing the number later, or a rider requesting a change of address or name later on. It is not allowed by the VAT law to reissue invoices for these reasons.

As for the data protection clauses, I can see that there is a clauses 11 ({{Supply of Contractor Services to Clients}}) and 13 ({{Introduction of Candidates to Clients for Direct Employment/Engagement}}) clarifying that Bolt and the counterparty are separate data controllers, and it's very short overall. In theory, this is not enough as per our internal practices, and our standard template would have to signed, or at least a few light touch controller clauses would have to be inserted to the agreement.

Here are the light touch clauses (please suggest the supplier to append this to clauses 13 and 11 referenced above)

# Each Party shall put in place adequate security measures to protect any personal information that it processes and shall not do, or omit to do, anything that would be in breach Applicable Data Protection Law.
#  Following the discovery of a personal data breach affecting data obtained in the context of this Agreement, the compromised Party shall notify the other Party without undue delay, and shall provide the other Party with a description and gravity of the personal data breach and its steps to rectify the data breach. 
# The [Supplier] hereby warrants, represents and undertakes that all personal data shared by it with Bolt, whether directly or indirectly, will be undertaken on the grounds of a valid lawful basis pursuant to Applicable Data Protection Law. The [Supplier] shall, at all times during and after the term of this Agreement, defend, hold harmless and indemnify (at its own expense) Bolt on demand against any claims, Loss, damages, costs or expenses and other liabilities (including but not limited to legal fees) incurred by Bolt arising out of or in connection with the sharing of personal data from the [Supplier] to Bolt.

The supplier is free to adopt the wording to reflect their contract (i.e. consistent terminology).

If they do not accept this change, I would say the risks are extremely minimal, as the basic clauses in their agreement would be formally enough. To clarify, for agreements between separate data controllers, there is no standard form that is strictly required, unless the transfer is outside of the EU/UK/adequate jurisdictions - which should be not the case here.







Also, I noticed the following restriction (4.6. of the {{Introduction of Candidates to Clients for Direct Employment/Engagement}}):

{{Client warrants that it shall not and shall procure that its employees and agents shall not, pass any information concerning a Candidate to any Third Party. Client acknowledges that Introductions of Candidates are confidential and that failure to comply with this clause 4.6 may cause Employment Agency to breach the Conduct Regulations and/or the Data Protection Laws and accordingly, Client agrees to indemnify Employment Agency from any and all liability in connection with Client’s breach of this clause 4.6.}}

Is this something that we can accept? Considering that {{“Third Party” means any company or person who is not Client. For the avoidance of doubt, subsidiary and}}
{{associated companies of Client (as defined by s.1159 of the Companies Act 2006 and s.416 of the Income and Corporation Taxes Act 1988 respectively) are included (without limitation) within this definition;}}

Hello, here's an update of the situation with HMRC regarding the top up payments after our discussions with Deloitte and the counsel.
*First about the application to get back the top up payments:*

* This decision from HMRC does not anyhow change our view of success in the main TOMS proceedings nor does it anyhow increase the chance that we would be hit with penalties for not paying the top up payments.
* We have to appeal this decision either in HMRC or in the First Tier Tribunal by June 26. Otherwise we will lose the opportunity to get these historic top up payments back. There is little use in contesting this in the HMRC so we are drafting grounds for appeal to the Tribunal.
* The general feeling is that there is little chance of getting the historic top up payments back in the near future if HMRC has chosen this hardball approach. We are discussing some interim relief application possibilities but there is not a lot of optimism from Deloitte about that. We are also in discussions with Deloitte if we could bring the hardship arguments to the play to help us but we need to discuss these possibilities a bit more.
* The most likely scenario is that our appeal will be stayed in the Tribunal until the main TOMS case is decided.

*Secondly about the threat that they will assess us for the top up payments that we haven't made from Q4*

* We are sending HMRC a reply where we question the urgency of making such assessments as per HMRC standard practice they would only make such assessments when the amounts would start to become out of time (year 2027 in our case).
* The reply will be quite strong worded but polite to match their tone of their Decision Letter. We'll make references to disproportional disadvantages that the HMRC approach would have on Bolt and that we would see the need to protect our position in the court.
* The aim is to get into discussion with them to get them to slow down with the assessments and wait until the main dispute is over. There are not a whole lot of instruments for us to use to make them stop making the assessments. So we have to rely on dialogue and presenting a strong case compared to the one of HMRC so they would not be keen on hurrying with the assessments as this would instantly open up a new front in our court battle.

HI

This is the result of the dynamic commission, the calculation of monthly commission does this way that  we are taking less commission from the driver because we are subtracting from the total Fee (App orders) - all bonuses/compensations/ride discounts

To calculate ride discounts ( need to export all orders for the same period and calculated the difference between the client payed and the ride price)

This is due to a new invoicing system we gradually started to adopt in mid-2022 called Dynamic Commission. Drivers' or Fleets' bonuses are now aggregated in their commission and the final sum is displayed only as one row: commission row. For example;

Commission: 100€, Bonuses 25€, Booking Fee 15€, Refunds 10€

Driver will only see a single row in their commission invoice in the amount of 50€ (100-25-15-10).

So, technically [actual commission - bounses/compensations - rider discounts - booking fees = commission on the invoice]

the report show the gross commission (the report shows the commission before all these discounts). on the invoice, the amount is all other things deducted from it (since commission netting is active). So actual commission invoice will never match with report.

Basically:

Commission invoice - the final sum of commission that  shows for the monthly period, how much commission we took from the driver in the end (after refunds, some of their bonuses/compensation, and rider discounts have been deducte- so this is Driver’s expenses this done to decrease Driver’s commission in the end.

But report and app expenses, shows gross amount that that driver owes to us before we deduct refunds/bonuses/compensations/ ride discounts. 

More info about dynamic commission [here|https://taxify.atlassian.net/wiki/spaces/COMM/pages/3663265890].

* To check rider discount ( need to get all finished orders from [Admin page|https://admin-panel.bolt.eu/ride-hailing-order/orders/export?filter=%7B%22limit%22%3A25%2C%22offset%22%3A0%2C%22filter%22%3A%7B%22start_timestamp%22%3A1718312400%2C%22end_timestamp%22%3A1718398799.999%2C%22all_order_try_states%22%3Afalse%7D%7D&tz=Europe%2FTallinn]  fro interesting period, the SUM up - columns Client paid and and sum up Ride price.  Rider discount = sum of client paid - sum Ride price



On your example;

The commission is 135.96 

Rider disc is - 69.54

Commission invoice = 135.96 - 69.54 = 66.42

*Data Subject Access Request – Response*

As you may be aware, the right of access under data protection law does not provide an individual with an absolute right of full access to any and all documents containing their personal data. For example, that right should not adversely affect the rights of others, including our trade secrets or intellectual property and in particular the copyright protecting the software.Furthermore, we must point out that if after careful analysis we conclude that our rights or rights of others prevail,  we will not be able to provide you with access to certain documentation where an exemption applies.

* The recipients or categories of recipients to whom the personal data has been or will be disclosed;

*Your rights*

If you have any additional questions, please contact our Customer Support Team by replying to this email.

 

 

Yours sincerely,



Bolt

Hi David,

I hope you’re doing well!
Bolt does not grant its employees shares, but stock options. Stock options act as a contract between you, the option holder, and Bolt, that has awarded you stock options. Having been awarded stock options means that you, as the option holder, have been given the right, but not the obligation, to buy a share of the company. Stock options themselves are not liquid, but these need to be exercised, i.e the strike price needs to be paid, and when doing that, stock options are converted into shares of the company.


The total vesting period of Bolt's grants is 4 years. Earn out steps happen every 3 months, and for first time grants there's a 1 year cliff in place. Taking this into account, it's hard to comment on what the person meant by saying that "shares only mean something if you have been at the company for two years". There's a Confluence page giving overview of [Bolt's option program|https://taxify.atlassian.net/wiki/spaces/BILP/pages/3748954176/Bolt+s+Option+Program]: important terms used, vesting schedules, what happens with stock options if one leaves Bolt and much more. On the same page you're able to find link to *Equity Compensation at Bolt* course in Seismic. Please let me know if you have any questions.



Kind regards

Hi Carolina! 
We see a couple of concerns here with this new category that is simple to abuse and hard for us to protect Bolt’s interests with the currently available methods. I understand that you are in a rush to go live but before you proceed further please have a look on the different aspects we would need to discuss further.

# *Predicting trip value*
One way we protect Bolt from customer debt and payment problems is through payment pre-authorisation for selected journeys. This basically means that upon booking the trip, we check if the customer can actually afford this or if their payment method is in working order. With this category set up, we would not know at the beginning of the journey what is the expected final pricing and could only assume the 35€ as the minimum charge, hence, as a result only be assured through pre-authorisation that the customer has the minimum amount available.
# *Limitless trips*
This brings us over to the second point that we have no way to ‘stop’ the journey. Let’s assume a scenario where a customer books a driver with this category, we do an initial check by booking 35€ from their payment method. Now, they go on to drive hours-on-hours (if we have removed all restrictions on destination changes) and end up with the final price of 300€. The customer does not have 300€ available and Bolt has only 35€ assurance so we are out 265€ that may never recover and will be difficult to recover. And as we allow the journey to proceed taking the risk of payment problems, then we may have to pay the driver from Bolt’s pocket essentially.
# *Who is this catered towards?*
Due to the previous concerns, we also have a clarification request on which customers are you intending on catching with this category. Should anyone and everyone in the area be able to use this category? As there are some concerning pitfalls here then perhaps we should consider only customers with trusted history to be eligible? What is your suspected GMV gain from this category?

To do a short conclusion then we see problematic areas in introducing this category without any controls or checks. In our experience, if we introduce a service with the potential for abuse, we will welcome and invite fraud as well. Therefore, I’d like us to be educated and considerate before proceeding further with going live.

Hey [~accountid:5acb1f48d8b95a2b34f150a8] 

We have received a Letter Before Court Action from two passengers who ordered a Bolt to London City Airport and have alleged that because the driver took a significantly longer route (which [~accountid:5f17f7301084620015f4972a] has confirmed did happen) they missed their flight. They are now seeking to claim £1,991.42 from Bolt as compensation for missing their package holiday. 

Irrespective of the driver taking a longer route, Bolt is not liable for compensating passengers if they miss any onward travel this is supported by our Passenger T&Cs. It is very likely that the passenger left their house later than they should have and are now trying to pin fault on Bolt. 

*The options available to the business are:* 

# Respond to the Letter Before Court Action referencing the T&Cs which state that Bolt is not liable, offer the passenger a gesture of goodwill and request that they seize any further proceedings against Bolt. 
# Settle the dispute by paying the passenger £1,991.42 and request that they seize any further proceedings against Bolt. 

Currently other than the driver taking a longer route which we have confirmed on our system did happen, the passengers have no other evidence to substantiate the other claims they have raised (for example: they allege that the driver was not in a fit state to drive and that the driver treated them in a particular way due to their sexuality). It is likely that the passengers are just trying to throw in some extra arguments as nothing to date has bee provided to Bolt to substantiate these allegations. 

Taking the above into consideration I think there is scope to argue against settling this dispute for the amount requested. However, please let me know which option you would prefer. If you decide option 1 can you please let me know the amount you would be willing to offer as a gesture of goodwill. 

Thank you.
